llm.summary: MeshMorize is a coherent local memory skill, but it asks agents to access transcript databases and rewrite automation payloads without clear consent or scoping.

dimensions.detail: Plaintext local memory is disclosed and mostly proportionate for a memory tool, but broad transcript-store inspection and automation-registry access are high-impact capabilities with insufficient limits.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is manual copying and PATH symlinking of local Python scripts; no remote payload retrieval or package dependency installation was found, but PATH-based invocation increases exposure to tool resolution issues.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to copy transcript SQLite files to /tmp/db-inspect, dump conversation windows, replay recovered words verbatim, and rewrite automation payloads when search is empty, without requiring explicit user confirmation or ownership checks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent plaintext logs, checkpoints, mesh files, and automation rewrites are central to the skill, but transcript copies under /tmp and verbatim recovered content can persist sensitive conversation data outside its original context.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The file-based memory, logging, search, checkpoints, and mesh functions match the stated purpose, but crash-gap recovery extends into host transcript databases and automation registry mutation beyond ordinary local memory files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable with plaintext local memory, and do not let it access transcript databases or automation registries unless you explicitly approve the exact session, time range, and job being read or changed. Avoid logging secrets or personal data, and clean up any temporary transcript copies.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: transcript recovery is related to memory restoration, but copying every matching transcript database to /tmp, dumping full event JSON, replaying words verbatim, and persisting recovered content is under-scoped for sensitive historical conversations.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: checking automations can be memory-adjacent, but listing, reading, and rewriting registry payloads based on search failure lacks ownership constraints, confirmation, and rollback guidance.
[T09] expected: Downgraded to a note in the overall verdict: memcheck uses shell=True with unqualified fixed commands, which is an unsafe local coding pattern, but I found no user-controlled command injection or hidden payload.
[SSD-3] expected: Partially accepted: persistent plaintext logging is disclosed and central to a memory skill, but the transcript recovery and verbatim replay guidance materially increases privacy risk.
[TP4] expected: Partially accepted as quality mismatch rather than malicious behavior: the artifact includes separate scripts for search and compliance, but the advertised five-day rotation is not fully implemented in bridge.py, which rotates only today, yesterday, and 2-days-ago.
